definitions.explanation: The entertainment district east of Shinjuku Station, packed with bars, restaurants, cinemas, host and hostess clubs, and neon signs. The name is used as shorthand for a loud, late-night, slightly disreputable part of town.

notes:
A neighborhood of {新宿区|しんじゅくく} in Tokyo. The name comes from a post-war plan to build a kabuki theater there; the theater was never built, but the name stuck.

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- ⟦{眠|ねむ}らない→眠る：01181_nemuru⟧⟦{街|まち}→街：17306_machi⟧: the city that never sleeps — a standard epithet for the district
- {歌舞伎町|かぶきちょう}{一番街|いちばんがい}: the main gate-marked street at its entrance
- ⟦ホスト→ホスト：25722_hosuto⟧⟦クラブ→クラブ：10812_kurabu⟧: host club — the business the district is most associated with

CULTURAL NOTE:
In conversation the name carries connotations of nightlife and of trouble: saying someone works or hangs around {歌舞伎町|かぶきちょう} implies a world of late hours and drinking. Despite the name, it has nothing to do with kabuki as a performing art — for that, see ⟦{歌舞伎|かぶき}→歌舞伎：04455_kabuki⟧.
